after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ given that $F(x,y)=(y\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,i+(x+y)\,j$ and $C$ is the path  $r(t)=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡t\,i+2j$ for $t\in [0,\frac{1}{2}].$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡t,\,y=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡t)\,i+(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡t+2)\,j \\  & =2t\,i+(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡t+2)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)j \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2t\,i+(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡t+2)\,j)\cdot (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\,i) \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{2t}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\,dt \\  & =-2\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}\,{|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =-2(\sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}-1) \\  & =2-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ given that $F(x,y,z)=\sqrt{x}\,i+\sqrt{y}\,j+z\,k$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=t\,i+t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [1,2].$
after.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x=t,\,y=t,\,z={t}^{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\sqrt{x}\,i+\sqrt{y}\,j+z\,k \\  & =\sqrt{t}\,i+\sqrt{t}\,j+{t}^{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =i+j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\sqrt{t}\,i+\sqrt{t}\,j+{t}^{2}\,k)\cdot (i+j+2t\,k) \\  & =\sqrt{t}+\sqrt{t}+2{t}^{3} \\  & =2\sqrt{t}+2{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{1}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(2\sqrt{t}+2{t}^{3})\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{4}{3}{t}^{3/2}+\frac{{t}^{4}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot 2\sqrt{2}+8-\frac{4}{3}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{16\sqrt{2}+37}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
